title: Isolation of T cells and dendritic cells from peripheral intestinal tissue, Peyer’s Patches and mesenteric lymph nodes in mice after intestinal manipulation
protocol: Induce and maintain anesthesia using isoflurane in oxygen.
Fix the mouse with its head away from the operator by taping its feet to the operating table.
Adjust direct halogen illumination to appropriate intensity for the operation.
Shave the abdomen using hair clippers and sterilize the skin with Kodan.
Make a 2 cm mid-line skin incision distally from the sternum.
Enter the peritoneal cavity via an incision along the linea alba made using a straight forceps and a sterile small scissor.
Keep the abdomen open with 2 retractors and place sterile moist cotton pads around the incision.
Carefully eventrate the small intestine with two saline-moistened cotton buds onto the sterile cotton pads.
Carefully unfold the small bowel loops on the cotton pads and run it once with moderate compression with two moist cotton buds from the oral to aboral direction.
Carefully replace the intestine back into the abdomen with moist cotton buds.
Complete surgical closure of the peritoneal cavity by two continuous sutures using the needle holder, straight forceps and suture material.
Terminate anesthesia and allow the animal to recover from the surgery under a heating lamp.
After 24 hours inspect the animal and wound closure for signs of infection or other complications.
Replace the animals under anesthesia using isoflurane in oxygen.
Kill the animal by cervical dislocation once under anesthesia to terminate anesthesia.
Reopen the abdomen using small scissors and straight forceps.
Clamp the abdominal aorta above the superior mesenteric artery and shortly above the aortic bifurcation.
Flush the aorta with 5 ml of cold (4 °C) sodium chloride (0.9%) to remove non-adherent blood cells from the vasculature.
Remove the complete GI tract by subdiaphragmatic transection of the esophagus and the colon at the most distal position accessible with a small scissor.
Sample any organ or tissue of interest for further studies during the removal process.
Place the GI tract in chilled KHB to inspect for integrity and absence of hematomas.
Remove the mesenteric lymph nodes from the GI tract placed in chilled KHB on ice.
Place the removed lymph nodes in chilled KHB on ice for further experiments.
Separate the colon from the jejunum/ileum.
Divide the jejunum/ileum or colon into 5 cm long segments using small scissors.
Fix the segment ends with small pins.
Transect the attaching mesentery using small scissors and straight forceps to unfold the organ completely.
Slip each segment over a glass rod (diameter 3 – 5 mm).
Scribe longitudinally along the muscularis layer with the branch of a straight forceps.
Strip the muscularis layer from the mucosa/submucosa layer using sterile cotton buds.
Collect stripped muscularis segments separately for small bowel and colon in 15 ml falcon tubes filled with chilled KHB.
Place tubes on ice.
Excise Peyer’s patches from the remaining mucosa layers still attached to the glass rod.
Place excised Peyer’s patches in chilled KHB on ice.
Remove the remaining mucosa/submucosa layer segments from the glass rod and collect them separately for small bowel and colon in 15 ml falcon tubes filled with chilled KHB.
Place these tubes on ice.
Centrifuge collected tissues at 500 g to remove the KHB supernatant if used for gene expression or protein analysis.
Transfer pellets into 1.5 ml cryotubes.
Snap-freeze the pellets in liquid nitrogen.
Store snap-frozen pellets at -80°C.
Pass the collected mesenteric lymph nodes through a 100 μm nylon mesh into a 15 ml tube filled with CMF/20% FCS by disrupting them mechanically on the mesh with a straight forceps.
Wash the collected cells and store them in CMF/20% FCS on ice until use.
Centrifuge the collected submucosa/mucosa segments at 500 g for 5 minutes at 4°C to remove the KHB supernatant.
Open the submucosa/mucosa tubes longitudinally with small scissors.
Wash the segments thoroughly before incubation in HBSS containing 2 mM EDTA for 15 minutes in a shaker at 37°C.
Shake the segments thoroughly in HBSS to remove the epithelial layer and mucus, repeating this process four times.
Incubate the remaining fragments of the mucosa/submucosa with 100 U/ml collagenase D and 30 μg/ml DNaseI in HBSS/20% FCS at 37°C for 45 minutes.
Disrupt the incubated fragments by shaking, collect the supernatants.
Repeat the process three times.
Pass the supernatant through a 100 μm Nylon mesh into a 50 ml tube.
Wash and store the filtered suspension in HBSS/20% FCS on ice until use.
Pool Peyer’s patches from each mouse and digest them with 100 U/ml collagenase D and 30 μg/ml DNaseI for 30 minutes.
Wash and store the digested material in HBSS/20% FCS on ice until use.
Centrifuge the collected muscularis segments at 500 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Cut the muscularis segments into smaller pieces under sterile conditions.
Incubate the muscularis pieces with 100 U/ml collagenase D and 30 µg/ml DNaseI in HBSS/20% FCS at 37°C for 45 minutes.
Disrupt the fragments by pipetting after incubation.
Pass the suspension through a 100 μm nylon mesh.
Wash the mesh with HBSS several times to clean it.
Digest muscularis fragments longer and repeat steps until all fragments pass through the mesh.
Wash the filtrated suspension with HBSS.
Centrifuge the suspension at 500 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Store the pellet on ice until use.
Incubate single-cell suspensions with 5 μg/10^7 cells Fc Block for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Wash the single-cell suspensions three times in PBS, centrifuging each time at 500 g for 5 minutes at 4°C and pipetting off supernatant completely.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 90 μl of buffer per 10^7 total cells.
Incubate single-cell suspensions with CD11c MicroBeads, CD3ε MicroBeads, CD4(L3T4) MicroBeads or CD8a (Ly-2) MicroBeads for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Wash single cell suspensions twice in PBS at 500 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Pipette off supernatant completely after each wash cycle.
Resuspend up to 10^8 cells in 500 μl buffer.
Perform MACS separation according to manufacturer’s recommendation.
Incubate the eventrated jejunum ex situ in a PBS solution with 10 µM CFSE for 10 minutes.
Wash the jejunum twice in PBS for 5 minutes to remove contaminating CFSE.
Produce single cell suspensions of the jejunum and colon as described.
Subject single cell suspensions to flow cytometry for CFSE positive cells.
Counterstain to detect T cells or dendritic cells.
